what_happened: While checking a flaky test by hand, the person running Athena ran cargo test in the repo. That left a 1.9 GB debug build in the repo's target folder and they did not clean it up. It was one of the things that pushed free disk below the 10 GB the batch needs. No job was involved.
cause: Disk is not managed as a budget. Athena does not compare free disk with the combined build size of running work, hand-run commands and kept build folders. Nothing makes a hand-run build and a drain share that budget, and nothing cleans up what hand runs leave behind. The limit shows up only when the free-disk guard fires, and a person must then free the space.
prevention: Add a disk-budget check to Athena. Before a drain batch starts, and before each stage, it would total the free disk against the expected build size of running and held work. It would also count stray target folders from hand runs. When space is short it would reclaim what is safe to reclaim, such as hand-run debug builds in the repo's target folder and the build folders of finished jobs. Otherwise it would report the exact folders and sizes to delete before work starts. Hand test runs would go through an Athena command that uses a throwaway target directory and removes it afterwards.
proposed_request: Make Athena manage free disk as a budget so hand-run builds cannot starve a drain batch. (1) Before a drain batch starts and before each stage, compute free disk against the 10 GB a writer needs plus the expected build size of running jobs. Also count stray build folders in the repo's target directory that no job owns. (2) When space is short, automatically delete what is safe to delete: build folders of finished or landed jobs and untracked hand-run target folders. Never delete a held job's own build. Log what was deleted and how much space it freed. (3) If space is still short after that, hold the batch before any job starts. The message must name each folder with its size. (4) Add `athena test-run`, a command that runs cargo test with a temporary target directory and removes it when it exits. Acceptance: a test shows that a 2 GB stray target folder is reclaimed before a batch starts and the batch then runs. A second test shows that a held job's build is never deleted. A third test shows the batch holds with a message listing folders and sizes when nothing can be reclaimed.
